children: HarbourVest Partners has raised $2.4 billion in initial closings for its new dedicated private-credit secondary strategy, according to people familiar with the fundraising.

The Boston-based firm-which operates in strategies like private credit, secondary transactions and co-investments-raised the capital across multiple vehicles, including a senior credit secondary fund and an opportunistic credit secondary vehicle, the people said.
They didn't say how much the firm is seeking for the strategy but did add that it plans to continue raising capital through 2027.

HarbourVest so far has deployed around $500 million across five transactions, including three that were general partner-led secondary deals and two transactions driven by sellers that are limited partners, the people said. It has a few hundred million dollars more in credit secondary deals in its pipeline, they added.

So-called GP-led deals, which have dominated most of the credit secondary market, allow asset managers to move a portfolio of loans into a new vehicle to give current investors a liquidity option while also extending the manager's ownership of the assets.

GP-led transactions accounted for some $17 billion of the $20.4 billion in total private-credit secondary volume during the first half of this year, according to a report from investment bank and advisory firm Evercore. The $20 billion in total private credit secondary volume was more than double the volume of private credit secondaries in the year-ago period, the Evercore report shows.

HarbourVest's LP-led deals included acquisitions of private-credit assets from sellers looking to unload multiasset portfolios. And its GP deals were structured as continuation vehicles that offered liquidity to investors in private credit funds facing fund life extensions, one of the people added.

Although the people didn't discuss specific transactions, early last month HarbourVest led the formation of a $730 million continuation vehicle deal for midmarket private-credit firm Willow Tree Credit Partners. The vehicle acquired a portfolio of around 130 securities, primarily first-lien loans and sponsor-backed companies, that Willow Tree had backed from a fund family it formed in late 2020 and early 2021.
HarbourVest's secondary team consists of 16 people, including 11 dedicated investment professionals, the people said.
HarbourVest's new credit secondary offering comes as liquidity pressure mounts on private-credit firms, including those structured as business-development companies and interval funds.

Shareholder redemptions from BDCs and interval funds have increased more than sixfold since the third quarter of 2025, according to Evercore. But so far traditional closed-end funds have driven much of the boost in GP-led deal volume, as private-credit firms look to generate cash from more mature funds, particularly those raised between 2018 and 2021, Evercore's report said.

But secondary investors have said they expect LP-led deals to increase over the next couple of years as pricing becomes more acceptable for sellers and limited partners become more familiar with the private-credit secondary market. LP-led credit secondary pricing for senior loans was 92% of net asset value in the first half of 2026, according to the Evercore report.

Earlier this year, in an interview on Bloomberg's Credit Edge podcast, HarbourVest Managing Director Greg Ciesielski, head of the credit secondary strategy, said that private-credit secondary volume could potentially reach $50 billion in 2026, more than double last year's volume.
